thread:
marta: heads-up — CI started failing on `infra:apply` for the payments namespace when we flipped the kms-module to v2. getting a decrypt error from the vectorizer pod immediately after rollout. not sure if it's a k8s annotation timing thing or terraform ordering. anyone seen this?

ian: can you paste the failing pod logs or the terraform plan/apply output? quick suspicion: grant or key policy didn't include the role ARN before the sa got annotated.

marta: logs from the pod error: `AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/irsa-payments@k8s.cluster-id/i-abcdef is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt`

marta: here's the relevant bits from the plan/apply (we only ran apply once, so ordering might be parallel):
```
module.kms.aws_kms_key.this: Creation complete
module.iam.aws_iam_role.irsa_payments: Creation complete
module.kms.aws_kms_grant.sa_decrypt[0]: Creation complete
module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.payments: Creation complete
module.k8s.kubernetes_service_account.payments: Creation complete (ID: payments)
```

marta: but the pod starts before the grant seems to be fully effective — timing window. CI doesn't retry the rollout.

devops-bot: CI job `infra:apply` ran 3m ago on runner-02, applied in parallel across modules (concurrency=4). Suggestion: add post-apply wait or plan/apply dependency.

kevin: common pattern: ensure the KMS key policy explicitly trusts the role principal (so grant is not the only authorization). Grants can be eventual/ephemeral; key policy is atomic. In TF that means you either: 1) attach the role ARN into the `aws_kms_key` policy document, or 2) add a strict `depends_on` from the grant to the role and serialize apply across modules.

kevin: small example (pseudo-terraform):
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "irsa_payments" { ... }
resource "aws_kms_key" "payments" { ... }
# ensure policy contains role ARN
data "aws_iam_role" "irsa_payments" { name = aws_iam_role.irsa_payments.name }
resource "aws_kms_key" "payments_with_policy" {
  policy = jsonencode({
    Version = "2012-10-17",
    Statement = [
      { Effect = "Allow", Principal = { AWS = data.aws_iam_role.irsa_payments.arn }, Action = "kms:*", Resource = "*" }
    ]
  })
}
```

kevin: or, if you want to keep grants, make sure the grant has `depends_on = [aws_iam_role.irsa_payments, kubernetes_service_account.payments]` so TF won't create the SA until grant/role are ready (or vice versa depending on what you pin).

marta: hmm we prefer not to modify key policy since these keys are shared across teams and policy churn is a bit scary. second approach seems safer. but cross-module depends_on is annoying. our modules are separate repos.

tara: another pragmatic option: after terraform apply, run a short custom check in CI that validates the key's effective policy/grants and then `kubectl rollout restart` the deployment if the service account can now decrypt. tiny script: try `aws kms decrypt` using token from pod SA (via `eks: get-token`) or curl an ephemeral pod. if failure, sleep & retry up to N.

marta: love that. would avoid changing tf structure. can you sketch the script?

tara: sure — conceptually:
```bash
# run in CI after terraform apply
kubectl -n payments run --rm -it debug --image=amazonlinux -- bash -c "aws sts get-caller-identity"
# or exec into a short-lived pod that uses the serviceaccount and run: aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://ct.bin --key-id alias/payments
# loop 10 times with 15s backoff, then if success: kubectl rollout restart deployment/vectorizer
```

ian: small note: use `kubectl wait --for=condition=Available deployment/vectorizer --timeout=120s` after restart. avoids noisy restarts in CI.

kevin: if you go the script route, also add a short tag to the terraform apply job to run with `concurrency: 1` for the kms/iam modules so we're less likely to hit race windows during large changes.

marta: thanks — I'll prototype the check-and-restart step in CI and slow down concurrency for kms/iam applies. will post the patch and ping for a quick review.

devops-bot: ticket created: INFRA-4821 — "kms apply ordering: add post-apply validation & rollout restart for payments" (assignee: marta).

marta: cool, leaving this to run on the next PR. pinging @kevin @tara for quick sanity check when I open the PR. :thumbsup:
